records.name: Veracruz de Ignacio de la Llave
records.summary:
The record's core practical-safety signal is the worst in the national data: this state led the national LGBT+ fatality count for four consecutive years — in 2021 alone, 10 recorded violent deaths of LGBT+ people, with 19 of 32 jurisdictions recording victims — and closed 2025 with at least 15 recorded hate crimes; the killing of a 27-year-old trans woman, stabbed to death in a motel on 19 November 2025, came after the state observatory had already counted nine hate crimes earlier that year, three of them against trans women, and the Coatzacoalcos-Oluta corridor is named in the national notes as this state's concentration zone. The danger inside the state is metro-and-corridor concentrated rather than uniform.

Legal protections and enforcement are absent in practice: before the 2025 civil-code gender-identity reform — among the last to be legislated — a visitor or resident had no legal route to correct gender documents, and there is no functioning investigation or prosecution machinery, distinct from other jurisdictions where laws exist but enforcement is weak. sources.summary: Letra S 'Muertes violentas de personas LGBT+ en México — Informe 2021' (May 2022): Veracruz led the national count of violent deaths of LGBT+ people for the fourth consecutive year, with 10 recorded cases in 2021, followed by Guanajuato (9), Estado de México (7) and Chihuahua (6); 19 of 32 states recorded victims. The report notes under-reporting: in a third of 2021 cases no name was published, and in 43 percent the sex recorded was male without attention to gender identity.
Diario de Xalapa (headline; body not extractable from cache): Veracruz closed 2025 with 15 recorded hate crimes against the LGBT community.

Jornada Veracruz: state prosecutor holds several open LGBT-murder files per activist Leonardo Ruiz (Orgullo Xalapa), including Edhibaldo Presa Parra, a Universidad Veracruzana professor found dead on 7 Jan; activists say hate-crime suspicion rests on motive patterns (avenaia, aggravants and the victim's orientation) and blame impunity in the FGE, while 'Soy Humano' data put 2024 below the national average.

LetraS Excela annual impunity report (7 May 2026): of 60 LGBT+ people murdered nationwide in 2025, 35 (58.3%) were trans women — a national trans-women homicide rate of 23.7 per 100,000. State ranking: Puebla 7, then Veracruz and Guanajuato 6 each; includes a Veracruz case (Oluta motel killing, Nov 2025).

records.name: Oaxaca
records.summary:
In May 2024 the organising brotherhood of a flagship traditional festival in this region circulated a written invitation stating that "men dressed as women will not be admitted"; activists filed a discrimination complaint with the national equality body, and the events are explicitly marketed to foreign tourists - the exclusion is directly visitor-facing.

Newer reporting profiles the region as a fastest-growing tourist paradise and at the same time its most dangerous for the LGBT+ community: several violent incidents are under investigation, in municipalities where armed groups operate, with possible municipal-police participation, and the official answer has been stepped-up visitor security rather than institutional reform.

The legal layer points the other way: the state has allowed legal gender recognition since 2019, extended it to age 12 and above by decree in 2021, and a 2023 Supreme Court ruling fully opened the procedure. sources.summary: La Tinta Oaxaca (25 May 2024): the organising brotherhood of the Vela San Vicente Ferrer Goola 'Lado Sur' festival in Juchitan circulated an invitation stating 'men dressed as women will not be admitted'; muxe activists, incl. defender Felina Santiago (three decades of advocacy), filed a discrimination complaint with the national equality body over the transphobic exclusion. Three velas went ahead on 26 May, with muxes affirming they are part of local society and culture.

Trendencias (Apr 2025): profiles Oaxaca as Mexico's fastest-growing tourist destination and simultaneously its most dangerous state for the LGBT+ community — violent incidents under investigation with possible municipal-police involvement in municipalities where armed groups operate; the murdered include muxe Cristian Hernandez Cutino (31) and stylist Zulma Hernandez Mendoza (43). State response has been stepped-up visitor security rather than institutional reform.

El Universal (27 Sep 2026): Oaxaca's human-rights ombudsperson (Defensoria) opened 34 investigations into attacks on LGBTIQ+ people between 2015 and 2022; violence against muxes persists — e.g. muxe teacher Marimar 'Estrellita' Santiago killed in 2022 on the road to Huilotepec, Istmo de Tehuantepec, prompting community demands for justice.

HRW 'Gender Recognition in Mexico by State' (11 Mar 2025), Oaxaca row: the 2019 state civil-code reform created an administrative legal-gender-recognition procedure, extended to age 12+ by decree in 2021, with a 2023 Supreme Court ruling fully opening the procedure — the documentary layer the summary's 'formally protective framework' claim rests on.
